q-124329.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119854/assets/77c069c4b4306b3337a44ddfc53ecd4d727e78da09d77d61e84fc01d3b30c302.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the closed path along the square of 
side $2,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, as shown above.
q-124329.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${x}_{1}={x}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Calculate ∫Cdy, where C=C1∪C2 is the path comprising of a vertical line segment of length 5 and a semicircle of radius 4, as shown above.

a

b
−5
c
2π+3
d

e

Correct
EXPLANATION

The line integral of unity with respect to y along a path C is equal to the net change in y between the terminal and initial points:

∫Cdy=y2−y1, where y2 is the y-coordinate of the terminal point, and y1 is the y-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, y1=4 and y2=−1. Therefore,

∫Cdy=y2−y1=(−1)−4=−5.

q-124187.worked_solution:
Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation.

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

In our case, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\ 17 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+5-{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\ 17 & =-7+5-{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\ 19 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-19.
$$
